claims.statement: The alerted cycle consists of four ACH transfers in Saudi Riyal between 50528/812D0C600 and 148350/812D0C3C0 over six days.
Account 50528/812D0C600 receives recurring payroll-like deposits from 223/811A83210 (cheques of 1,244.94 and card payments of 727.89) multiple times per week.
Both alerted accounts transact heavily with 148350/811FFF630, sending and receiving large ACH amounts.

findings.narrative: The cycle alert fired on four ACH transfers between accounts 50528/812D0C600 and 148350/812D0C3C0 over six days. Both accounts show ordinary business activity: 812D0C600 receives regular payroll-like deposits from 223/811A83210 (cheques of 1,244.94 and card payments of 727.89 recurring multiple times per week) and a large cheque deposit of 255,267.17 from 149340/812838660. Both accounts transact heavily with 148350/811FFF630 (large ACH flows in both directions). The two alerted accounts share this common counterparty and also settle balances with each other. The four cycle transfers (8677, 10301, 11221, 19698) are irregular amounts on different days, not structured, and fit the pattern of inter-company or supplier payments between related entities banking at the same institution. No laundering indicators such as rapid layering, round-number splitting, or unusual counterparties are present.
